title: Story Generator — Arabic Therapy Stories
text:
The Story Generator uses a locally-hosted Qwen 2.5 language model to generate child-safe, fully vocalized Arabic stories that embed target therapy words. It enables therapists and parents to create personalized, engaging reading materials specifically tuned to a child’s current speech therapy targets.
All inference is 100% offline — no internet connection is required after the initial model download.

title: Story Generator — Arabic Therapy Stories
text:
Clinical Purpose
Story-based therapy is a research-backed technique for generalizing speech production gains. By embedding target words in a narrative context:

Children encounter the phoneme in natural, meaningful contexts
Repeated exposure across the story reinforces motor pattern consolidation
The vocalization (tashkeel / حركات) makes the text readable for young learners
Stories follow everyday themes familiar to Palestinian children

title: Story Generator — Arabic Therapy Stories
text:
Story Generation Pipeline

System Prompt Engineering
The LLM is constrained by a carefully engineered Arabic system prompt that enforces:

Simplified vocabulary — age-appropriate for children 3–7
Full vocalization (tashkeel) — critical for correct Arabic reading
Target word embedding — wrapped in parentheses (قطار) for visibility
Cultural safety — no religious, violent, or adult content
Everyday themes — playground, school morning, colored blocks

title: Story Generator — Arabic Therapy Stories
text:
Full Source Code



Code

Story_Generator.py

import os
import gradio as gr
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import torch

LOCAL_MODEL_PATH = "./qwen_text_model"

if not os.path.exists(LOCAL_MODEL_PATH) or not os.listdir(LOCAL_MODEL_PATH):
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Local text model folder is empty! Run the download script first."
    )

print("Loading Qwen Text Model offline...")
device      = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
torch_dtype = torch.float16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(LOCAL_MODEL_PATH)
model     = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    LOCAL_MODEL_PATH,
    torch_dtype=torch_dtype,
    device_map=device
)
print(f"Story Generator loaded on {device.upper()}!")


def generate_safe_story(target_words: str, story_theme: str) -> str:
    if not target_words.strip():
        return "Please enter target words first."

    system_prompt = (
        "أنت كاتب محترف لقصص الأطفال الصغار جداً، وتكتب باللغة العربية الفصحى المبسطة "
        "والمشكولة بالكامل (بالحركات).\n"
        "مهمتك: كتابة قصة قصيرة جداً، بسيطة، تدور حول أحداث يومية عادية يفهمها الطفل الصغير.\n"
        "شروط صارمة:\n"
        "1. تجنب المفاهيم الأخلاقية أو الدينية أو الفلسفية العميقة.\n"
        "2. لا محتوى للبالغين أو عنف أو أفكار مخيفة.\n"
        "3. ادمج الكلمات المستهدفة بشكل متكرر وطبيعي داخل السرد.\n"
        "4. ضع الكلمات المستهدفة بين قوسين مثل: (عصفور)، (قطار) في كل مرة تظهر."
    )

    user_prompt = (
        f"السياق العام للقصة: {story_theme}\n"
        f"الكلمات المستهدفة (ضعها بين قوسين وكررها): {target_words}"
    )

    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
        {"role": "user",   "content": user_prompt}
    ]

    text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        messages,
        tokenize=False,
        add_generation_prompt=True
    )

    model_inputs = tokenizer([text], return_tensors="pt").to(device)

    with torch.no_grad():
        generated_ids = model.generate(
            **model_inputs,
            max_new_tokens=800,
            temperature=0.6,  # Low temperature = strict, predictable output
            top_p=0.9
        )

    generated_ids = [
        output_ids[len(input_ids):]
        for input_ids, output_ids in zip(model_inputs.input_ids, generated_ids)
    ]

    return tokenizer.batch_decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)[0]


# Gradio Interface
with gr.Blocks(title="Arabic Children's Story Generator (Offline)") as demo:
    gr.Markdown("# 📚 Arabic Therapy Story Generator — Offline")
    gr.Markdown(
        "Generates simple, vocalized Arabic stories for children, "
        "with therapy target words embedded and highlighted."
    )

    with gr.Row():
        with gr.Column():
            gr.Markdown("### Story Settings")
            words_input = gr.Textbox(
                label="Target Words (comma-separated)",
                placeholder="e.g.: عصفور، قطار",
                lines=2
            )
            theme_input = gr.Dropdown(
                choices=[
                    "يوم جميل وممتع في الحديقة العامة",
                    "اللعب بالألعاب الجميلة في غرفتي",
                    "ذهاب الطفل إلى المدرسة صباحاً ومشاهدة الطريق",
                    "مساعدة الأم في ترتيب المكعبات الملونة"
                ],
                value="يوم جميل وممتع في الحديقة العامة",
                label="Story Theme"
            )
            generate_btn = gr.Button("Generate Story", variant="primary")

        with gr.Column():
            gr.Markdown("### Generated Story")
            story_output = gr.Textbox(
                label="Vocalized Arabic Story",
                lines=15,
                placeholder="Story will appear here..."
            )

    generate_btn.click(
        fn=generate_safe_story,
        inputs=[words_input, theme_input],
        outputs=story_output
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.launch()

title: Qwen3 ASR — Advanced Speech Recognition
text:
The Qwen3 ASR Module is an advanced speech-to-text engine that goes beyond basic transcription. It uses the Qwen3-ASR model running fully offline to produce:

High-accuracy Arabic transcription
Word-level timestamps — exact start/end time for each spoken word
Bilingual support — Arabic and English in a single interface

Word-level timestamps are clinically significant: they allow therapists to identify hesitations, prolongations, and phoneme insertion points — patterns critical for stuttering and fluency disorder assessment.

title: Qwen3 ASR — Advanced Speech Recognition
text:
Full Source Code



Code

Qwen3-ASR.py

import os
import gradio as gr
from qwen_asr import Qwen3ASRModel
import torch

LOCAL_MODEL_PATH = "./qwen_model"

if not os.path.exists(LOCAL_MODEL_PATH) or not os.listdir(LOCAL_MODEL_PATH):
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Local model folder is empty! Please run the download script first."
    )

print("Loading Qwen3-ASR model from local folder...")
device      = "cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
torch_dtype = torch.float16 if torch.cuda.is_available() else torch.float32

model = Qwen3ASRModel.from_pretrained(
    LOCAL_MODEL_PATH,
    dtype=torch_dtype,
    device_map=device,
    trust_remote_code=True
)
print(f"Model loaded on {device.upper()}!")


def format_timestamps(results) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Parse Qwen3 ASR output into text + word-level timeline."""
    if isinstance(results, list) and len(results) > 0:
        results = results[0]

    text_out = getattr(results, "text", "")
    time_out = ""

    if hasattr(results, "words") and results.words:
        lines = []
        for w in results.words:
            word  = getattr(w, "word",  "")
            start = getattr(w, "start", 0.0)
            end   = getattr(w, "end",   0.0)
            lines.append(f"⏱️ [{start:05.2f}s → {end:05.2f}s] : {word}")
        time_out = "\n".join(lines)
    else:
        time_out = "No timestamps returned. Ensure clean audio input."

    return text_out, time_out


def process_audio(audio_source, mic_file, uploaded_file, language) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Route audio from microphone or file upload to the ASR model."""
    active_file = mic_file if audio_source == "Microphone" else uploaded_file

    if not active_file:
        return "❌ No audio provided.", "Please record or upload audio first."

    try:
        lang_tag = "Arabic" if language == "Arabic" else "English"
        results  = model.transcribe(audio=active_file, language=lang_tag)
        return format_timestamps(results)

    except Exception as e:
        return "❌ Error.", f"Exception: {str(e)}"


# Gradio Interface
with gr.Blocks(title="Qwen3 Advanced ASR — Offline") as demo:
    gr.Markdown("# 🔬 Qwen3 ASR — Word-Level Timestamped Transcription")
    gr.Markdown(
        "Advanced offline speech recognition with word-level timestamps. "
        "Supports **Arabic** and **English** audio input."
    )

    with gr.Row():
        source_toggle = gr.Radio(
            choices=["Microphone", "File Upload"],
            value="Microphone",
            label="Audio Source"
        )
        language_selector = gr.Dropdown(
            choices=["Arabic", "English"],
            value="Arabic",
            label="Language"
        )

    with gr.Row():
        mic_input  = gr.Audio(sources=["microphone"], type="filepath", label="Microphone")
        file_input = gr.Audio(sources=["upload"],     type="filepath", label="Upload Audio")

    analyze_btn = gr.Button("Analyze Speech 🔬", variant="primary")

    with gr.Row():
        text_output = gr.Textbox(label="Full Transcription",        lines=4)
        time_output = gr.Textbox(label="Word-Level Timeline",       lines=10)

    analyze_btn.click(
        fn=process_audio,
        inputs=[source_toggle, mic_input, file_input, language_selector],
        outputs=[text_output, time_output]
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.launch(share=True)

title: Maze Craze — Gamification Layer
text:
Maze Craze is the gamification layer of the rehabilitation platform. It wraps speech therapy exercises inside an engaging, browser-based maze game built with Phaser 3 — a professional HTML5 game framework.
Children navigate a maze character to collect coins and reach the goal. The game is designed as a reward wrapper around therapy sessions — correct pronunciation unlocks movement or rewards, creating positive reinforcement loops.
Two versions exist: v1 (classic grid maze) and v2 (enhanced with assets and improved UI).

title: Maze Craze — Gamification Layer
text:
Gamification Rationale






NoteWhy Games?



Research in pediatric speech therapy consistently shows that intrinsic motivation dramatically improves therapy adherence and generalization. Children who play while practicing show 2-3x higher session engagement compared to drill-based approaches.


Key design principles: - Immediate feedback — visual/audio rewards on correct production - Progressive difficulty — maze complexity increases with performance - Character selection — agency and personalization increase buy-in - Zero reading required — icon-based UI accessible to preliterate children

title: AI-Driven Arabic Speech Rehabilitation Platform
text:
Communication is a fundamental human right and a critical vector for cognitive, social, and emotional development. Pediatric communication disorders present unique developmental hurdles that, if left unaddressed, can lead to permanent academic and social marginalization.
This project integrates computer vision, speech signal processing, and generative AI to deliver an accessible, automated, and dialect-aware rehabilitation tool tailored for Palestinian children.

This project integrates computer vision, speech signal processing, and generative AI to deliver an accessible, automated, and dialect-aware rehabilitation tool tailored for Palestinian children.

title: AI-Driven Arabic Speech Rehabilitation Platform
text:
The Problem
In Palestine, pediatric communication disorders pose a severe public health crisis. Children suffering from disorders such as:

Childhood Apraxia of Speech (CAS)
Verbal stuttering
Phonological deletion
Environmental language delays

…face profound barriers to social integration.
The core issue lies in a compounding deficit of:







Barrier
Description




Clinical Shortages
Acute shortage of certified Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs)


Geographical Barriers
Infrastructure centralized in urban centers; rural families face prohibitive transport costs


Dialectal Void
AI tools built for Western languages or MSA — not Palestinian/Levantine dialect

title: AI-Driven Arabic Speech Rehabilitation Platform
text:
Local Statistics (Palestine)






ImportantKey Data — Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics (PCBS)




Communication disabilities are the 2nd most prevalent childhood disability in Palestine — 37.3% of all pediatric disability cases
West Bank: 35.7% — Gaza Strip: 40.1%
Jenin Governorate (AAUP home region): highest disability rate in the West Bank at 4.1% of the total population
Rural children face an Odds Ratio (OR) of 4.4 risk of prolonged speech delays due to low income
Congenital factors account for 33.6% of communication disabilities

title: AI-Driven Arabic Speech Rehabilitation Platform
text:
Module Overview


Saif — Lip Vision
Real-time Childhood Apraxia of Speech (CAS) assessment using MediaPipe Face Mesh.
Calculates the Lip Pucker Ratio (LPR) to track jaw drops and lip-rounding.
View Details →


Layla — Speech Analysis
Arabic phonological analysis and fluency detection using OpenAI Whisper.

title: Saif Module — Lip Apraxia Vision
text:
The Saif Module is the computer vision core of the platform. It targets children diagnosed with Childhood Apraxia of Speech (CAS) — a neurological disorder where the brain struggles to plan and coordinate the precise oral movements needed for speech.
The module uses MediaPipe Face Mesh to extract 3D facial landmarks from a live webcam feed and continuously evaluates the child’s lip geometry against clinical articulatory targets.

title: Saif Module — Lip Apraxia Vision
text:
The Saif Module is the computer vision core of the platform. It targets children diagnosed with Childhood Apraxia of Speech (CAS) — a neurological disorder where the brain struggles to plan and coordinate the precise oral movements needed for speech.
The module uses MediaPipe Face Mesh to extract 3D facial landmarks from a live webcam feed and continuously evaluates the child’s lip geometry against clinical articulatory targets.

title: Saif Module — Lip Apraxia Vision
section: Clinical Foundation — The Digital DTTC Protocol
text:
Clinical Foundation — The Digital DTTC Protocol
The module implements a software adaptation of the Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing (DTTC) protocol, a gold-standard clinical technique for treating CAS. The core metric is the Lip Pucker Ratio (LPR):
\[
\text{LPR} = \frac{d_{\text{horizontal}}}{d_{\text{vertical}} + \epsilon}
\]
Where:

\(d_{\text{horizontal}}\) = pixel distance between left and right lip corners (landmarks 61 → 291)
\(d_{\text{vertical}}\) = pixel distance between upper and lower lip midpoints (landmarks 13 → 14)
\(\epsilon = 0.001\) — prevents division by zero


LPR Decision Logic



LPR Condition
Clinical State
Feedback




\(d_v \leq 12\) px
Mouth fully closed
✅ Letter B / M — Correct


\(\text{LPR} < 1.8\)
Rounded pucker
✅ Letter O / W — Correct


\(d_v > 35\) px
Mouth fully open
✅ Letter A — Correct


Otherwise
Incorrect motor plan
❌ Retry!

title: Saif Module — Lip Apraxia Vision
text:
Full Source Code



Code

lips_prototype.py

import cv2
import mediapipe as mp
import math

# Initialize MediaPipe Face Mesh
mp_face_mesh = mp.solutions.face_mesh
face_mesh = mp_face_mesh.FaceMesh(
    max_num_faces=1,
    refine_landmarks=True,
    min_detection_confidence=0.5,
    min_tracking_confidence=0.5
)

# Standard Mouth Landmark IDs
LIP_TOP    = 13
LIP_BOTTOM = 14
LIP_LEFT   = 61
LIP_RIGHT  = 291

# Start Webcam
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)
print("Webcam started. Press [ESC] or [Q] to close.")

while cap.isOpened():
    success, frame = cap.read()
    if not success:
        continue

    # Mirror the frame naturally for the child
    frame = cv2.flip(frame, 1)
    h, w, _ = frame.shape

    rgb_frame = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    results = face_mesh.process(rgb_frame)

    status_text = "Status: Waiting for action..."
    color = (255, 255, 255)

    if results.multi_face_landmarks:
        for face_landmarks in results.multi_face_landmarks:

            # Extract landmark coordinates
            pt_top    = face_landmarks.landmark[LIP_TOP]
            pt_bottom = face_landmarks.landmark[LIP_BOTTOM]
            pt_left   = face_landmarks.landmark[LIP_LEFT]
            pt_right  = face_landmarks.landmark[LIP_RIGHT]

            # Convert normalized values to pixel coordinates
            y_top,    x_top    = int(pt_top.y * h),    int(pt_top.x * w)
            y_bottom, x_bottom = int(pt_bottom.y * h), int(pt_bottom.x * w)
            y_left,   x_left   = int(pt_left.y * h),   int(pt_left.x * w)
            y_right,  x_right  = int(pt_right.y * h),  int(pt_right.x * w)

            # Geometric calculations for Apraxia tracking
            vertical_dist   = math.sqrt((x_top - x_bottom)**2 + (y_top - y_bottom)**2)
            horizontal_dist = math.sqrt((x_left - x_right)**2 + (y_left - y_right)**2)
            lip_ratio       = horizontal_dist / (vertical_dist + 0.001)

            # Clinical Evaluation
            if vertical_dist <= 12:
                status_text = "GOAL - CLOSED: MOUTH CLOSED (Letter: B / M)"
                color = (0, 255, 0)
            elif lip_ratio < 1.8:
                status_text = "GOAL - ROUNDED: LIPS ROUNDED (Letter: O / W)"
                color = (0, 255, 0)
            elif vertical_dist > 35:
                status_text = "GOAL - OPEN: MOUTH OPEN (Letter: A)"
                color = (0, 255, 0)
            else:
                status_text = "ALERT: Incorrect Planning - Retry!"
                color = (0, 0, 255)

            # Draw augmented overlay on the child's mouth
            for (x, y) in [(x_top, y_top), (x_bottom, y_bottom),
                           (x_left, y_left), (x_right, y_right)]:
                cv2.circle(frame, (x, y), 4, color, -1)
            cv2.line(frame, (x_top, y_top), (x_bottom, y_bottom), (255, 0, 0), 1)
            cv2.line(frame, (x_left, y_left), (x_right, y_right), (255, 0, 0), 1)

    cv2.putText(frame, status_text, (20, 40),
                cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, color, 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
    cv2.imshow('Smart Speech Therapy - AI Camera Unit', frame)

    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF in [27, ord('q')]:
        break

cap.release()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

title: Multimodal System
text:
The Multimodal System is the most technically complex module in the platform. It fuses the Lip Apraxia Vision engine (Saif) and the Whisper Speech-to-Text engine (Layla) into a single, thread-safe, real-time application.
The system processes two simultaneous data streams: 1. Video stream — MediaPipe extracts 3D lip landmarks from the webcam at ~30 fps 2. Audio stream — Whisper transcribes the child’s recorded speech
Both streams run on separate threads to prevent blocking, managed by a centralized thread-safe state object.

title: Multimodal System
text:
Thread-Safe State Management


Code
import threading
from collections import deque
import time

class ThreadSafeState:
    """Prevents race conditions between the video and audio threads."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._status = "Initializing..."
        self._confidence_history = deque(maxlen=CONFIG.SMOOTHING_WINDOW)
        self._last_update = time.time()
        self._frame_count = 0
        self._fps = 0.0

    @property
    def status(self) -> str:
        with self._lock: return self._status

    @status.setter
    def status(self, value: str):
        with self._lock:
            self._status = value
            self._last_update = time.time()

    @property
    def mouth_correct(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if 60%+ of recent frames show correct mouth shape."""
        with self._lock:
            if len(self._confidence_history) < 3: return False
            return sum(self._confidence_history) / len(self._confidence_history) > 0.6

    def update_mouth_state(self, is_correct: bool):
        with self._lock:
            self._confidence_history.append(1.0 if is_correct else 0.0)

state = ThreadSafeState()

title: Multimodal System
text:
Model Manager


Code
import whisper
import mediapipe as mp
import torch
import threading

class ModelManager:
    """Initializes and safely shares Whisper + MediaPipe models across threads."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self._device = self._detect_device()
        self.whisper_model = self._init_whisper()
        self.face_mesh     = self._init_mediapipe()

    def _detect_device(self) -> str:
        if torch.cuda.is_available(): return "cuda"
        if hasattr(torch.backends, "mps") and torch.backends.mps.is_available(): return "mps"
        return "cpu"

    def _init_whisper(self):
        try:
            model = whisper.load_model(CONFIG.WHISPER_MODEL_SIZE, device=self._device)
            print(f"✅ Whisper loaded on {self._device.upper()}")
            return model
        except Exception:
            print("⚠️ Falling back to CPU for Whisper")
            self._device = "cpu"
            return whisper.load_model(CONFIG.WHISPER_MODEL_SIZE, device="cpu")

    def _init_mediapipe(self):
        mp_face_mesh = mp.solutions.face_mesh
        # refine_landmarks=False disables iris tracking — major speedup
        return mp_face_mesh.FaceMesh(
            max_num_faces=CONFIG.MAX_FACES,
            refine_landmarks=False,
            min_detection_confidence=CONFIG.MIN_DETECTION_CONFIDENCE,
            min_tracking_confidence=CONFIG.MIN_TRACKING_CONFIDENCE
        )

    def process_frame(self, rgb_frame):
        with self.lock: return self.face_mesh.process(rgb_frame)

    def transcribe(self, audio_path: str) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            return self.whisper_model.transcribe(
                audio_path,
                language=CONFIG.WHISPER_LANGUAGE,
                fp16=(self._device == "cuda"),
                condition_on_previous_text=False,  # Prevents hallucination
                no_speech_threshold=0.6,
                initial_prompt=CONFIG.TARGET_WORD  # Focus on target
            )

models = ModelManager()

title: Layla Module — Speech-to-Text Analysis
text:
The Layla Module is the acoustic analysis engine of the platform. It uses OpenAI Whisper to transcribe children’s Arabic speech in real time and performs phonological error classification — detecting specific patterns such as phoneme deletion, substitution, and fluency breakdown.
The module is designed around Palestinian/Levantine dialect phonology, targeting common errors in disorders like phonological deletion (e.g., dropping the initial /q/ in “قطار” → “طار”) and verbal stuttering.

speech_prototype.py

import gradio as gr
import whisper
import torch

# 1. Detect GPU and load model on best available device
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
print(f"Loading Whisper model on ({device})...")

# Base model — optimal balance between speed and Arabic phoneme accuracy
model = whisper.load_model("base", device=device)
print("Model loaded successfully!")

# 2. Define the target word for the current therapy session
TARGET_WORD = "قطار"  # Example: "Qitar" (Train)

def check_arabic_speech(audio_file_path):
    if not audio_file_path:
        return "⚠️ Please press the microphone and record your voice first!"

    try:
        # 3. Run Whisper with forced Arabic language decoding
        # language="ar" prevents transliteration to Latin script
        result = model.transcribe(audio_file_path, language="ar", task="transcribe")
        transcribed_text = result["text"].strip()

        # 4. Normalize: remove punctuation, keep alphanumeric + spaces
        clean_text = "".join(
            c for c in transcribed_text if c.isalnum() or c.isspace()
        ).strip()

        # 5. Phonological analysis and clinical feedback
        if clean_text == TARGET_WORD:
            return f"✅ Excellent! Correct pronunciation 100%!\nSpoken word: [{clean_text}]"

        # Detect initial phoneme deletion (child says طار instead of قطار)
        elif "طار" in clean_text or "تتار" in clean_text:
            return (
                f"❌ Phonological deletion detected (initial consonant dropped)!\n"
                f"Spoken: [{clean_text}]\n"
                f"Guidance: Try producing the /q/ sound forcefully from the back of the throat."
            )

        else:
            return (
                f"❌ Pronunciation does not match target.\n"
                f"Heard: [{clean_text}]\n"
                f"Target: [{TARGET_WORD}]"
            )

    except Exception as e:
        return f"Error processing audio signal: {str(e)}"


# 6. Build the Gradio interactive interface
with gr.Blocks(title="Smart Speech Therapy - AI Audio Unit") as demo:
    gr.Markdown("# 🎤 Real-Time Arabic Speech Analysis (AI)")
    gr.Markdown(f"### 🎯 Current Challenge: Pronounce the word **[{TARGET_WORD}]** clearly")

    with gr.Row():
        audio_input = gr.Audio(
            sources=["microphone"],
            type="filepath",
            label="Press the microphone and start speaking"
        )

    with gr.Row():
        check_btn = gr.Button("Analyze Speech 🚀", variant="primary")

    with gr.Row():
        output_result = gr.Textbox(
            label="Phonological Analysis Result",
            lines=4
        )

    check_btn.click(fn=check_arabic_speech, inputs=audio_input, outputs=output_result)

# 7. Launch with share=True for mobile microphone access
if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.launch(share=True)

import os
import soundfile as sf
import gradio as gr
import torch
from habibi_tts.infer.utils_infer import HabibiTTS

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Load the unified multi-dialect TTS engine
tts_engine = HabibiTTS(model_type="Unified", device=device)


def generate_arabic_speech(text, dialect):
    """Convert Arabic text to speech using the selected dialect."""
    if not text.strip():
        return None

    out_path = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "output.wav")

    # Run inference
    audio, sr = tts_engine.infer(gen_text=text, dialect=dialect)

    # Convert tensor to numpy array if needed
    if isinstance(audio, torch.Tensor):
        audio = audio.cpu().numpy()

    # Save to WAV file
    sf.write(out_path, audio, sr)
    return out_path


# Build the Gradio interface
with gr.Blocks(title="Habibi-TTS Arabic Speech Synthesis") as demo:
    gr.Markdown("# 🔊 Habibi-TTS — Dialect-Aware Arabic Speech")
    gr.Markdown("Enter Arabic text and select a dialect to synthesize natural speech.")

    with gr.Row():
        text_input = gr.Textbox(
            label="Arabic Text",
            lines=5,
            placeholder="أدخل النص العربي هنا..."
        )
        dialect_input = gr.Dropdown(
            choices=["MSA", "EGY", "LEV", "SAU", "UAE"],
            value="LEV",
            label="Dialect"
        )

    with gr.Row():
        audio_output = gr.Audio(label="Generated Speech", type="filepath")

    btn = gr.Button("Generate Speech 🎙️", variant="primary")
    btn.click(generate_arabic_speech, [text_input, dialect_input], audio_output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.launch(share=True)
